source: segmentation (Blender simulation, background replaced by pure white)
units: pixels (x right, y down, origin top-left) and seconds; t = frame/24
view: top-down (bird's-eye) view of two cars on a plane; no ground texture or markings (background pure white RGB 255)

camera.motion: assumed static (simulation convention); background is blank so pan cannot be checked directly. Van heading stays at 90.0 +/- 0.3 deg and car heading settles at 0.0 deg, no rotation of the frame; both cars' sizes constant (no zoom).
camera.perspective: none usable; orthographic-looking top view, both cars at the same depth (same ground plane)

objects.name: white_van
objects.description: white/light-grey van/minivan with dark-red windscreen and red side windows, left object, front pointing up (toward smaller y)
objects.motion: straight line upward (-y), x constant ~831.5; starts essentially at rest at frame 0 and speeds up steadily (step grows ~0.3 px/frame per frame, from ~0.5 px/frame to ~19.5 px/frame at frame 71)

size_px.note: length is vertical (front-rear), width horizontal; top view so 'height' is not observable

objects.name: beige_car
objects.description: beige / light pink-tan car with a rounded body, initially right of the van and slightly ahead (front up), turns right to face +x
objects.motion: starts moving at frame 1, nearly constant speed (~6.8 px/frame, per-frame steps 5.8-7.8 from mask noise) along a clockwise (right-hand) quarter-circle turn: heading 90 deg (up) at frames 0-2 to 0 deg (right, +x) at ~frame 65, then straight to the right

static_objects: none (no ground features, markings or props visible; background replaced)

events.event: white_van at (near) rest, begins accelerating upward; first steps 0.2-1.5 px
beige_car starts moving (step 0->1 = 0.5 px, step 1->2 = 5.7 px; full speed from frame 2)
beige_car begins turning right (heading leaves 90 deg)
beige_car heading reaches ~0 deg (turn complete), continues straight in +x
last frame; no contact between the cars at any time (separate masks in all 72 frames)
